html:
The Hualapai, also spelled Walapai, are an Indigenous people of northwest Arizona, along the south rim of the western Grand Canyon. Their name means "people of the tall pines". They speak a Yuman language shared with their close relatives the Havasupai.

They lived in small bands, hunting and gathering across a wide plateau and farming at springs. When miners and ranchers came in the 1860s, the Hualapai fought them in a war that lasted until about 1870. In 1874 the army marched them south to La Paz on the Colorado River, where many died; they later escaped and returned. A reservation was set up in 1883. Today the tribe runs tourism at the canyon, including the glass Skywalk. Their neighbours include the Yavapai.
